The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, condemning the illegal and inhumane actions and measures taken by the US government to disrupt Iran’s commercial exchanges and air transportation with other countries through the extraterritorial implementation of illegal US sanctions, stresses that these measures not only run counter to the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, particularly the principle of respect for the national sovereignty of states, and violate fundamental human rights standards, but also constitute a dangerous plot aimed at undermining friendly relations among countries, particularly neighboring states. In this regard, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, recalling the deep historical, religious, cultural and people-to-people ties between the two nations of Iran and Iraq, and appreciating the fraternal relations and good-neighborly ties between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Republic of Iraq, considers the imposed restrictions on civil air travel between Iran and Iraq to be contrary to the common interests and objectives of the two countries. Relations between Iran and Iraq go beyond the conventional relations between two neighboring countries and are founded on deep people-to-people ties and mutual interests in various fields. The travel of millions of Iranian and Iraqi citizens for economic and commercial activities, pilgrimage to holy sites, tourism, education, and medical treatment necessitates that issues related to transportation and communications between the two nations be managed independently, responsibly and with a forward-looking approach, based on their common interests. The restrictions imposed on air travel between the two countries, in addition to creating serious difficulties for hundreds of thousands of passengers, pilgrims, patients, students and economic actors from the two countries, are in clear contradiction with the nature of the strategic relations and good-neighborly ties between Iran and Iraq. While respecting the national sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq, the Islamic Republic of Iran calls for appropriate decisions to be taken in response to the US economic terrorism and sedition-mongering with a view to lifting the restrictions and restoring normal conditions for flights operated by the airlines of the two countries, in line with the interests and objectives of the two nations.

item.title: Iran urges Canada to answer for fate of indigenous children unmarked graves
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmil Baghaei, in a post on X marking Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, called on the Canadian government to provide evidence, transparency and accountability regarding the fate of Indigenous children and unmarked graves linked to the country’s residential school system. That question still haunts the conscience of the world when it comes to the Canada's Indigenous children who were taken from their families, stripped of their names, languages, cultures, and identities, and subjected to a system of forced assimilation. Many suffered abuse and neglect, and many died far from home and buried in unmarked graves. September 30 was Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation - apparently to honour residential school survivors and their families, and to remember the innocent Indigenous children who never came home. But reconciliation cannot be reduced to a commemorative day or political rhetoric. When serious questions remain unanswered and the history of residential schools is contested or obscured, reconciliation remains incomplete. The suffering of Indigenous children is not a culture war. It is a matter of historical truth and accountability. Questions surrounding unmarked graves deserve evidence, transparency, and an honest examination of the historical record - not denial, distortion, or silence. No reconciliation without truth. No justice without accountability.

item.title: Baghaei: Nihilism in US governance poses grave threat to human life and civilization
item.description: In a post on X, Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baghaei warned that “structural nihilism” in the US system of governance poses a grave threat to human life and civilization, criticizing indifference to the consequences of military aggression against Iran. "In the end we all die anyway, so it doesn't matter." This is no conventional political statement; it echoes Albert Camus’s Caligula at the exact moment existential 'absurdity' curdles into tyranny - where the 'inevitability of death' is used to strip the living of their value. Because life ends, Caligula reasoned, the suffering of others is inconsequential. The terrifying difference today is leverage. Caligula had only the primitive tools of Rome; modern nihilism commands vast stockpiles of mass destruction. The greatest geopolitical danger is not a leader confronting mortality. It is a system that uses the inevitability of death to justify indifference to human suffering. “We all die” is a fact; “so it doesn't matter” is the leap where existential dread becomes a political weapon. Those who think they can appease Caligula forget that the absurd recognizes no rule or contract. Appeasement buys no safety - it merely negotiates the order of the victims.

item.title: Iranian Japanese Foreign Ministers hold phone conversation
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held a phone conversation at noon on Thursday. During the phone conversation, the two sides exchanged views on Tehran-Tokyo bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister elaborated on Iran’s positions and views regarding the situation in the region, stressing that the continued insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf region is solely the result of the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, and that the only way to restore security is to stop the US’s illegal activities. Araghchi also explained the good offices by some mediators to advance the diplomatic process, stressing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to defend its interests. The Japanese Foreign Minister, for his part, elaborated on Japan’s views regarding matters of common interest.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, on the final day of his trip. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister outlined the latest developments in the West Asia region following the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran, stressing that the Islamic Republic of Iran, as a founding member of the United Nations, has expected and continues to expect the Organization and its member states not to remain indifferent to the violation of law and gross breaches of the Charter by a permanent member of the Security Council, and to explicitly condemn the continuation of the United States’ unlawful interventionist measures and threats. Referring to the two rounds of unlawful US and Israeli attacks against Iran in the midst of negotiations within less than one year, as well as the continuation of acts of aggression in the form of a naval blockade and economic terrorism, the Foreign Minister stressed Iran’s determination to defend its national sovereignty and territorial integrity with all its capabilities. He stated that the Iranian nation will never abandon its demand for justice and for the prosecution and punishment of those who ordered and perpetrated the war crimes committed by the United States and the Israeli regime. Recalling Iran’s responsible approach toward international peace and security, Araghchi noted that the Islamic Republic of Iran has always remained steadfast in its commitment to using diplomacy as a means of safeguarding its national interests and ensuring peace in the region. However, he said, the United States has repeatedly betrayed diplomacy over the past decade and, by violating its commitments, has contributed to insecurity in the region. Araghchi also referred to the continuation of the Israeli regime’s genocide and warmongering in the occupied Palestinian territories, Lebanon, Syria and other countries in the region, and recalled the responsibility of the United Nations and the Security Council to end Israel’s impunity and halt the crimes being committed in Gaza and the West Bank. The UN Secretary-General, condemning violations of the fundamental principles of the Charter, particularly the use of force by superpowers, stressed the need for all countries to abide by the principles and rules of international law and to use diplomacy to resolve issues. The meeting also addressed the continued gross violations by the United States of the Host Country Agreement and its obstruction of the normal activities of Iran’s Mission. Iran’s protest over the performance of the host government in this regard was conveyed to the Secretary-General, who was urged to take the necessary measures to compel the US government to fulfill its obligations.
